This chapter executes independently, rebuilding the shared cleaning, frozen
split and logistic benchmark from the supplied data. It asks how alternative
models change predicted default risk and lending decisions on the same loans.

**Python adaptation.** The single tree uses scikit-learn CART on treatment-coded
predictors. R's `rpart` can group several factor levels in a split and uses a
relative misclassification cost-complexity parameter. Scikit-learn searches
individual encoded columns and has a different pruning criterion. Here the
depth and minimum sample restrictions are explicit, with no cost-complexity
pruning. Consequently the tree, leaf IDs and predictions differ. Its own
computed results support the interpretations below.

XGBoost preserves the objective, features, 160 rounds, learning rate and other
model settings. The installed Python and R library versions differ. The seed
1049419804 is the engine seed recorded by the R fit after `set.seed(567)`;
Python passes that value directly. It was taken from R's saved configuration,
before examining alternative seeds. Comparisons use the same test borrowers.

```{python}
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter,MaxNLocator,FuncFormatter
from scipy.special import expit,logit
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score,log_loss
import xgboost as xgb
from IPython.display import display,Markdown
from shared.output import setup,show_table,show_figure,finish,BLUE,RED,GREEN
from shared.scoring import load_data,fit_logistic,design,metrics,policy,strategy,calibration,display_frame
from shared.scoring_figures import distributions,roc_plot,calibration_plot,COLORS
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tree_helpers',Path('chapters/02-tree-based/helpers/models.py'))
helpers = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(helpers)
figure_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tree_figures',Path('chapters/02-tree-based/helpers/figures.py'))
tree_figures = importlib.util.module_from_spec(figure_spec)
figure_spec.loader.exec_module(tree_figures)
out = setup('02-tree-based')
_,_,clean,train,test,_ = load_data()
models,logistic_pred = fit_logistic(train,test)
y = test.loan_st.to_numpy(int)
ytrain = train.loan_st.to_numpy(int)
xtrain,xtest = design(train,intercept=False),design(test,intercept=False)
```

## 2.2 A single decision tree

```{python}
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
tree = DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion='gini',max_depth=4,min_samples_split=100,
                              min_samples_leaf=33,ccp_alpha=0,random_state=567)
tree.fit(xtrain,ytrain)
pred_tree = tree.predict_proba(xtest)[:,1]
print('Terminal leaves:',tree.get_n_leaves(),'Distinct test PDs:',len(np.unique(pred_tree)))
```

### Figure 2.1 {#result-figure-2-1}
```{python}
show_figure(out,'2.1',tree_figures.tree_figure(tree,list(xtrain.columns)))
```

The shared root is shown above two panels, one for each root branch, so all
nodes remain readable. Within each panel the left branch satisfies the displayed
condition and the right branch does not. The terminal boxes are leaves. Each assigns its training default proportion
to every test borrower reaching it. Internal nodes only route borrowers.
Scikit-learn numbers nodes in depth-first order, including both internal nodes
and leaves; the leaf IDs in the next table refer directly to this figure.

### Table 2.1 {#result-table-2-1}
```{python}
leaves = helpers.leaf_rules(tree,list(xtrain.columns))
test_leaf = tree.apply(xtest)
leaves['Test loans'] = [int(np.sum(test_leaf==i)) for i in leaves.Leaf]
leaves['Test default rate'] = [float(y[test_leaf==i].mean()) if np.any(test_leaf==i) else np.nan
                              for i in leaves.Leaf]
show_table(out,'2.1',leaves)
```

### Table 2.2 {#result-table-2-2}
```{python}
tree_metrics = metrics(pred_tree,y)
show_table(out,'2.2',pd.DataFrame({'Quantity':['Terminal leaves','Distinct test PDs','Minimum PD','Maximum PD','AUC','Brier score'],
    'Value':[tree.get_n_leaves(),len(np.unique(pred_tree)),pred_tree.min(),pred_tree.max(),
             tree_metrics['auc'],tree_metrics['brier_score']]}))
```


### Table 2.4 {#result-table-2-4}
```{python}
show_table(out,'2.4',pd.DataFrame({'Matrix':['Training','Test'],'Rows':[len(xtrain),len(xtest)],
                                 'Encoded predictors':[xtrain.shape[1],xtest.shape[1]]}))
print('Encoded columns:',', '.join(xtrain.columns))
```

```{python}
dtrain = xgb.DMatrix(xtrain,label=ytrain,nthread=1)
dtest = xgb.DMatrix(xtest,label=y,nthread=1)
base_pd = float(ytrain.mean())
base_margin = logit(base_pd)
params = dict(objective='binary:logistic',eval_metric=['logloss','auc'],max_depth=3,
              eta=.05,subsample=.8,colsample_bytree=.8,min_child_weight=20,
              reg_lambda=1,base_score=base_pd,seed=1049419804,nthread=1,tree_method='hist')
history = {}
booster = xgb.train(params,dtrain,num_boost_round=160,evals=[(dtrain,'train'),(dtest,'test')],
                    evals_result=history,verbose_eval=False)
pred_xgb = booster.predict(dtest)
pred_xgb_train = booster.predict(dtrain)
rounds,scores,path_pd,case_indices = helpers.checkpoint_paths(booster,dtest,y,base_pd)
case_names = ['Default case','Non-default case']
checkpoints = [0,5,20,60,100,160]
```

### Table 2.5 {#result-table-2-5}
```{python}
show_table(out,'2.5',pd.DataFrame([
    ['Objective',params['objective'],'Binary default probabilities'],
    ['Maximum depth',3,'Limits interactions in each tree'],
    ['Learning rate (eta)',.05,'Scales each new correction'],
    ['Row fraction',.8,'Samples training rows per tree'],
    ['Column fraction',.8,'Samples encoded predictors per tree'],
    ['Minimum child weight',20,'Minimum summed curvature weights (Hessians) p(1-p) in each child, not an applicant count'],
    ['L2 penalty (lambda)',1,'Regularizes leaf corrections'],
    ['Initial PD',base_pd,'Training default rate'],
    ['Boosting rounds',160,'Fixed model length; not selected using these test results'],
    ['Engine seed',1049419804,'Same effective seed recorded in the R model configuration']],
    columns=['Setting','Value','Role']))
```

The two illustrative cases use the R companion's selection rule: among observed
defaults with rising final PD and non-defaults with falling final PD, select
the largest log-loss improvement plus 0.05 times the total checkpoint score
movement. Their identities may change across implementations. This selection
illustrates successful corrections; overall model quality is evaluated later
over the entire test set.

```{python}
path_rows = []
for name,i in zip(case_names,case_indices):
    previous_score,previous_round = base_margin,0
    for r in checkpoints:
        j = rounds.index(r)
        path_rows.append({'Case':name,'Checkpoint':f'{r} (+{r-previous_round} trees)',

show_table(out,'2.7',pd.DataFrame(path_rows))
```

### Table 2.8 {#result-table-2-8}
```{python}
individual_loss = lambda outcome,p: -(outcome*np.log(p)+(1-outcome)*np.log1p(-p))
loss_rows = []
for name,i in zip(case_names,case_indices):
    initial = individual_loss(y[i],base_pd)
    final = individual_loss(y[i],pred_xgb[i])
    loss_rows.append({'Case':name,'Observed default':y[i],'Initial PD':base_pd,
        'PD at round 5':path_pd[i,rounds.index(5)],'Final PD':pred_xgb[i],
        'Initial log-loss':initial,'Final log-loss':final,'Loss reduction':initial-final})
show_table(out,'2.8',pd.DataFrame(loss_rows))
```

### Table 2.9 {#result-table-2-9}
```{python}
applicant_index = case_indices[0]  # Zero-based position; profile displays this value + 1.
applicant = xgb.DMatrix(xtest.iloc[[applicant_index]],nthread=1)
leaf_ids = booster.predict(applicant,pred_leaf=True)[0].astype(int)
tree_dump = booster.trees_to_dataframe()
def leaf_value(round_number,leaf_id):
    hit = tree_dump[(tree_dump.Tree==round_number-1)&(tree_dump.Node==leaf_id)&(tree_dump.Feature=='Leaf')]
    assert len(hit)==1
    return float(hit.Gain.iloc[0])
leaf_values = np.array([leaf_value(r,leaf_ids[r-1]) for r in range(1,6)])
first_scores = np.array([booster.predict(applicant,output_margin=True,iteration_range=(0,r))[0]
                         for r in range(1,6)])
np.testing.assert_allclose(base_margin+np.cumsum(leaf_values),first_scores,atol=5e-7,rtol=2e-6)
arithmetic = [
    ['Select applicant',f'xtest.iloc[[{applicant_index}]]',f'Test position {applicant_index+1}; file row {test.index[applicant_index]}'],
    ['Initial PD','ytrain.mean()',base_pd],
    ['Initial score',r'$F_0=\log[p_0/(1-p_0)]$',base_margin]]
previous = base_margin
for r in [1,2]:
    delta = leaf_values[r-1]
    arithmetic.extend([
        [f'Round {r}: leaf',f'booster.predict(applicant, pred_leaf=True)[0, {r-1}]',int(leaf_ids[r-1])],
        [f'Round {r}: correction',f'leaf_value({r}, {leaf_ids[r-1]})',delta],
        [f'Round {r}: updated score',f'$F_{r} = {previous:.6f} + ({delta:.6f})$',first_scores[r-1]],
        [f'Round {r}: updated PD',f'$p_{r} = 1/[1+\exp(-F_{r})]$',expit(first_scores[r-1])]])
    previous = first_scores[r-1]
show_table(out,'2.9',pd.DataFrame(arithmetic,columns=['Step','Code or calculation','Result']))
```

`pred_leaf=True` returns an applicant-by-tree matrix. Row 0 refers to the single
selected applicant, and column 0 to the first tree. The leaf correction read
from the dump already includes the learning rate; adding it directly avoids
applying eta twice. The assertion checks this arithmetic against the model's
own predicted score.

### Table 2.10 {#result-table-2-10}
```{python}
show_table(out,'2.10',pd.DataFrame({'Round':range(1,6),'Leaf ID':leaf_ids[:5],
    'Previous score':np.r_[base_margin,first_scores[:-1]],'Leaf correction':leaf_values,
    'Updated score':first_scores,'Updated PD':expit(first_scores)}))
```

## 2.4 Estimation and final predictions

The estimation call above fits 160 trees once. Checkpoints use prefixes of that
same ensemble through `iteration_range=(0, rounds)`. The first bound is inclusive
and the second exclusive. A separate test verifies that these prefixes agree
with a shorter fit using the same settings and seed.

A gap describes performance on these two samples. A late deterioration in test
AUC while training AUC rises is evidence worth investigating, but a single
curve cannot establish performance on future lending cohorts. The test curve
here is descriptive; an operational round count should be chosen on separate
validation data before the final test evaluation.

## 2.5 Understanding the fitted ensemble

### Figure 2.6 {#result-figure-2-6}
```{python}
gain = pd.Series(booster.get_score(importance_type='total_gain')).reindex(xtrain.columns,fill_value=0)
gain = gain/gain.sum()
top = gain.nlargest(12).sort_values()
fig,ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7,5))
ax.barh(top.index,top.values,color=BLUE)
ax.set_xlabel('Share of total split gain')
fig.tight_layout()
show_figure(out,'2.6',fig)
```

### Figure 2.7 {#result-figure-2-7}
```{python}
shap = helpers.contributions(booster,dtest)
mean_abs_shap = pd.Series(np.mean(np.abs(shap[:,:-1]),axis=0),index=xtrain.columns)
top = mean_abs_shap.nlargest(12).sort_values()
fig,ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7,5))
ax.barh(top.index,top.values,color=BLUE)
ax.set_xlabel('Mean absolute contribution (log-odds units)')
fig.tight_layout()
show_figure(out,'2.7',fig)
```

Split gain measures reductions in the training objective. Mean absolute
contributions measure the magnitude of each feature's allocated contribution
to test-set scores. They answer different questions, so their rankings can differ.

### Figure 2.8 {#result-figure-2-8}
```{python}
pdp = helpers.partial_dependence(booster,test)
fig,axes = plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(12,4),sharey=True)
for ax,var,label in zip(axes,['int','income','age'],['Interest rate (%)','Annual income ($)','Age']):
    d = pdp[pdp.variable==var]
    ax.plot(d.value,d.average_predicted_pd,color=BLUE,lw=2)
    ax.set_xlabel(label)
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(4))
    if var=='income': ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v,pos:f'${v/1000:.0f}k'))
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1))
axes[0].set_ylabel('Average predicted PD')
fig.tight_layout()
show_figure(out,'2.8',fig)
```

At each grid point the code replaces one predictor for every test borrower,
rebuilds the encoded matrix and averages predicted PDs. This is a model-based
summary. Correlated characteristics may make some replacements atypical, so
the curve should be interpreted as model sensitivity rather than a causal effect.

## 2.6 Comparing models and lending strategies

```{python}
predictions = {'logi_full':logistic_pred['full'],'single_tree':pred_tree,'xgboost':pred_xgb}
model_metrics = pd.DataFrame([dict(model=k,**metrics(p,y)) for k,p in predictions.items()])
strategies = pd.concat([strategy(p,y).assign(model=k) for k,p in predictions.items()],ignore_index=True)
cal = {k:calibration(predictions[k],y,test.index) for k in ['logi_full','xgboost']}
best_by_model = strategies.loc[strategies.groupby('model').net_payoff.idxmax()].copy()
best_overall = best_by_model.loc[best_by_model.net_payoff.idxmax()]
```

```{python}
        -5*best_overall.accepted_defaults,best_overall.net_payoff]}))
```
